missing: Actual product picks: which current power banks have a printed Wh rating under 100Wh (around 20,000-26,800mAh). Each should be checked against the 2026 airline rules: one bank on Southwest, two under ICAO, no recharging in flight. Each pick needs a current price, plus the trade-off between usable capacity and charging speed.
why: Authorities fill the results: FAA, IATA, Southwest and American Airlines. But they only cover the rules (100Wh and 160Wh limits, carry-on only, the 2026 changes). None of them names or tests a power bank. No major reviewer appears. The two non-authority pages are explainers on the rules, also with no products. So nobody answers 'which power bank is best and allowed on the plane'. The open slot is a product page built around compliance: picks under 100Wh with a clearly printed Wh label, current prices, and a table of rules by airline. One risk: ChatGPT searched in a rules-heavy way, so the page has to state the 2026 rules clearly to rank for that kind of query.
